intro.title: RBAC Permission Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable custom hook in Angular that checks user permissions based on Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). You will learn how to use Angular's dependency injection and RxJS to create a service that provides role data and a hook that consumes it to conditionally render UI elements. The main technologies involved are Angular services, TypeScript interfaces, and RxJS Observables for reactive state management. By the end, you'll have a functional permission hook that can be used to secure parts of your application based on user roles.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications like enterprise dashboards or admin panels, different users (e.g., admins, managers, regular users) need to see and interact with different UI elements based on their roles. For instance, an admin might see a 'Delete User' button or a 'System Settings' menu option, while a regular user does not. Implementing an RBAC permission hook allows developers to cleanly encapsulate this logic, conditionally rendering buttons, forms, or entire dashboard sections without cluttering components with repetitive permission checks. This pattern is essential for building secure, maintainable applications where UI visibility and functionality must dynamically adapt to user permissions.
